{"passages":[{"reference":"2.33","text":"When these things had been said in this way, the good Peter himself also began to speak:

“Brothers, you must grasp the truth of the rule of pairing, from which anyone who does not depart cannot be led astray. For since, as we said, we see that all things are arranged twofold and in opposition—first night, then day; first ignorance, then knowledge; and first disease, then healing—so the things of error come into life first, and only afterward does the truth come upon it, as the physician comes upon the disease. For instance, when our God-loving nation was about to be delivered from its mistreatment by the Egyptians, first the diseases arose through the staff that had been turned into a snake, the staff given to Aaron, and only afterward were the healings brought about through Moses’s prayers. And now too, when the nations are about to be delivered from the religion of idols, evil once again, acting in advance as though it itself were reigning, first sent its own ally, like a snake—the Simon whom you see—who performs wonders for astonishment and deception, not healing signs for turning and salvation. You must therefore discern from the marvels being performed those who perform them: which person is whose worker. If someone performs useless marvels, he is a servant of evil; but if he does beneficial things, he is a leader belonging to the good.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τοῦ τῆς συζυγίας κανόνος","chosen":"the rule of pairing","rationale":"συζυγία denotes a coupling or paired arrangement and here introduces the author’s pattern of opposed pairs."},{"source_quote":"δυϊκῶς καὶ ἐναντίως","chosen":"twofold and in opposition","rationale":"Preserves both the division into two and the opposition between the members."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ θεοφιλοῦς ἡμῶν ἔθνους","chosen":"our God-loving nation","rationale":"θεοφιλής can describe one who loves God or one beloved by God; the main rendering follows its active sense while the alternative remains possible."},{"source_quote":"τῆς ὀφιωθείσης ῥάβδου","chosen":"the staff that had been turned into a snake","rationale":"ὀφιόω presents the staff as having been made serpent-like or transformed into a snake."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς ἐπιστροφὴν καὶ σωτηρίαν","chosen":"for turning and salvation","rationale":"ἐπιστροφή is a turning or return; it is distinct from μετάνοια, and the Greek does not explicitly supply a destination."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ ἐστὶν ἡγεμών","chosen":"he is a leader belonging to the good","rationale":"ἡγεμών means leader or guide. The genitive τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ may mean either ‘of the good’ or ‘of the Good One’; the main text preserves the formally neuter reading."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ ἐστὶν ἡγεμών","issue":"The substantival genitive τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ can be understood as neuter, ‘the good,’ or masculine, ‘the Good One.’ The main rendering adopts the former without excluding a personified or divine referent.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"2.34","text":"Accordingly, the useless signs are all the things that you yourselves have said Simon performed. I mean his making statues walk, his rolling on burning coals, his becoming a dragon, being transformed into a goat, flying into the air, and whatever other things there are of this kind. Since they are not done for the healing of human beings, they are naturally apt to deceive many besides. The signs of compassionate truth, however, are benevolent: you heard that the Lord had performed them and that I, after him, accomplish them through prayers. Most of you have been present for these—some freed from diseases of every kind, others from demons; some having had their hands straightened, others their feet; some having recovered their eyes, others their hearing—and for all the other things a person can do once he has come to belong to a benevolent spirit.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"προσαπατᾶν φύσιν ἔχει πολλούς","chosen":"they are naturally apt to deceive many besides","rationale":"The idiom φύσιν ἔχει marks a natural tendency, while the prefix in προσαπατάω can suggest deceiving additional people as well."},{"source_quote":"τὰ δὲ τῆς οἰκτίρμονος ἀληθείας σημεῖά ἐστι φιλάνθρωπα","chosen":"The signs of compassionate truth, however, are benevolent","rationale":"The genitive associates the signs with truth, while φιλάνθρωπα describes them as humane or benevolent toward people."},{"source_quote":"κἀμὲ μετ’ ἐκεῖνον εὐχαῖς κατορθοῦντα","chosen":"that I, after him, accomplish them through prayers","rationale":"μετ’ ἐκεῖνον places Peter after the Lord, and κατορθόω presents the acts as successfully accomplished."},{"source_quote":"οἱ δὲ τὰς ἀκοὰς","chosen":"others their hearing","rationale":"The participle ἀπολαβόντες, ‘having recovered,’ is carried forward elliptically from the preceding clause."},{"source_quote":"φιλανθρώπου πνεύματος ἴδιος γενόμενος","chosen":"once he has come to belong to a benevolent spirit","rationale":"ἴδιος with a genitive can describe someone as belonging to or being the own possession of another. ‘A benevolent spirit’ is retained without deciding whether the author intends the divine Spirit."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"οἱ δὲ τὰς ἀκοὰς καὶ ἄλλα ὅσα ἄνθρωπος ποιεῖν δύναται, φιλανθρώπου πνεύματος ἴδιος γενόμενος","issue":"After the repeated οἱ δέ clauses, καὶ ἄλλα has no newly expressed governing verb. It may continue the broader signs for which the audience was present or resume the things Peter accomplishes. The translation attaches it to the witnessed signs; the concluding masculine participle clearly qualifies ἄνθρωπος.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"2.35","text":"After Peter had said these things, Zacchaeus came in to us toward daybreak, greeted us, and said to Peter:

“Simon postpones the debate until tomorrow, for today happens to be his sabbath, the one occurring every eleven days.”

Peter answered him, “Tell Simon, ‘Carry it through as you wish, knowing that we are ready to meet you whenever you wish, by God-loving providence.’”

After hearing this, Zacchaeus went out to give the reply in return.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Ἀνατίθεται Σίμων τὴν ζήτησιν","chosen":"Simon postpones the debate","rationale":"ἀνατίθεται here means that Simon puts off or defers the scheduled disputation."},{"source_quote":"τὸ δι’ ἕνδεκα ἡμερῶν αὐτοῦ τυγχάνει σάββατον","chosen":"happens to be his sabbath, the one occurring every eleven days","rationale":"διά with the temporal expression is taken as marking an interval. ‘His sabbath after eleven days’ is also formally possible."},{"source_quote":"Ἐπιτέλει ὡς θέλεις","chosen":"Carry it through as you wish","rationale":"ἐπιτελέω can mean complete, perform, or observe. The omitted object may be the sabbath observance or Simon’s intended course of action, so the English leaves the reference contextually open."},{"source_quote":"θεοφιλεῖ προνοίᾳ","chosen":"by God-loving providence","rationale":"The adjective is preserved directly. It may alternatively mean ‘God-beloved’ or ‘dear to God,’ though that produces an equally unusual description of providence."},{"source_quote":"ἀντιβάλλειν τὴν ἀπόκρισιν","chosen":"to give the reply in return","rationale":"The compound verb conveys returning or delivering an answer in response."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"2.36","text":"Seeing that I was disheartened, he asked the reason and learned from me that it came from nowhere else than the postponement of the debate. He said:

“Anyone who has taken it as a prior conviction that the world is governed by God’s good providence, Clement, my friend, is not himself distressed over circumstances that arise however they may, having acknowledged that under the administration of the superior one circumstances reach their outcome beneficially. Therefore, because he recognizes the superior one as just and lives with a good conscience, he knows how to shake from his soul, by sound reasoning, the painful event that befalls him, since it is bound to come about through some unknown good agency. And now, do not let Simon the magician’s postponement of the debate distress you; for perhaps it has happened through God’s providence for your benefit. Therefore, since you are one of my own, I will not hesitate to tell you.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὁ προειληφὼς διοικεῖσθαι τὸν κόσμον","chosen":"Anyone who has taken it as a prior conviction that the world is governed","rationale":"προλαμβάνω here describes grasping or accepting something beforehand as a governing premise."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τῆς τοῦ κρείττονος οἰκονομίας","chosen":"under the administration of the superior one","rationale":"οἰκονομία denotes ordering or administration, while the substantival comparative τοῦ κρείττονος may refer to God as the superior one or higher power."},{"source_quote":"δίκαιον αὐτὸν εἶναι γνοὺς","chosen":"because he recognizes the superior one as just","rationale":"The pronoun most naturally resumes ‘the superior one.’ A reflexive sense, ‘recognizes himself as righteous,’ is less likely because the Greek does not use a reflexive pronoun."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς ἀγαθοῦ τινὸς ἀγνώστου συντελούμενον ἐλθεῖν ἔχει","chosen":"it is bound to come about through some unknown good agency","rationale":"With the genitive, πρός can mark source or agency, and συντελούμενον presents the event as being brought about. Context could instead encourage the teleological sense ‘for the sake of some unknown good.’"},{"source_quote":"ὡς ἰδίῳ σοι ὄντι","chosen":"since you are one of my own","rationale":"ἴδιος describes Clement as personally belonging to Peter’s intimate circle, rather than merely receiving private information."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τὰ·πράγματα","issue":"The printed middle dot falls between the article and its noun, where it cannot function as normal sentence punctuation. The translation reads the continuous phrase while preserving the wording itself.","proposed_reading":"τὰ πράγματα","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"πρὸς ἀγαθοῦ τινὸς ἀγνώστου συντελούμενον ἐλθεῖν ἔχει","issue":"The genitive after πρός supports source or agency, yielding ‘through some unknown good agency,’ but the providential argument also permits an intended teleological sense, ‘for the sake of some unknown good.’ Both are defensible without changing the printed text.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
